title.zh: 卷89 酷吏:于洛侯 胡泥 李洪之 高遵張赦提 羊祉 崔暹 郦道元
title.en: Volume 89: Cruel Officals - Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Gaozun Zhang Sheti, Yang Zhi, Cui Xian, Li Dao Yun
title.raw: 卷89 酷吏:于洛侯 胡泥 李洪之 高遵張赦提 羊祉 崔暹 郦道元 Volume 89: Cruel Officals - Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Gaozun Zhang Sheti, Yang Zhi, Cui Xian, Li Dao Yun

sentences.zh: 于洛侯 胡泥 李洪之 高遵 張赦提 羊祉 崔暹 酈道元 谷楷

translations.literal: Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Gao Zun, Zhang Sheti, Yang Zhi, Cui Xian, Li Daoyuan, Gu Kai
translations.idiomatic: Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Gao Zun, Zhang Sheti, Yang Zhi, Cui Xian, Li Daoyuan, and Gu Kai

sentences.zh: 淳風既喪，姦黠萌生；

translations.literal: When pure customs were already lost, treachery and cunning sprouted forth;
translations.idiomatic: Once honest ways had decayed, deceit and cunning took root;

sentences.zh: 法令滋章，刑禁多設。

translations.literal: Laws and ordinances proliferated, punishments and prohibitions were set up in great number.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes multiplied, and penal restrictions were imposed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 為吏罕仁恕之誠，當官以威猛為濟。

translations.literal: As officials they rarely had sincerity in kindness and forbearance; holding office they took fierceness and might as their means.
translations.idiomatic: Officials seldom showed genuine mercy; in office they relied on brute force to get things done.

sentences.zh: 魏氏以戎馬定王業，武功平海內，治任刑罰，肅厲為本，猛酷之倫，所以列之今史。

translations.literal: The Wei clan by military horses fixed their royal enterprise, by martial achievement pacified the sea within, governed relying on punishments, took severity and austerity as foundation — hence these fierce and cruel sorts are listed in this present history.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei house won its throne by the sword and pacified the realm by force; their rule rested on penal law and stern discipline, which is why these men of savage cruelty are recorded in this history.

sentences.zh: 于洛侯，代人也。

translations.literal: Yu Luohou was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Luohou was from Dai.

sentences.zh: 以勞舊為秦州刺史，而貪酷安忍。

translations.literal: By merit of long service he was made Governor of Qin Province, yet he was greedy, cruel, and calmly endured cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded for long service with the governorship of Qin Province, he proved greedy, brutal, and utterly pitiless.

sentences.zh: 州人富熾奪民呂勝脛纏一具，洛侯輒鞭富熾一百，截其右腕。

translations.literal: A man of the province, Fu Chi, seized from the commoner Lü Sheng one set of shin-guards; Luohou immediately flogged Fu Chi one hundred strokes and cut off his right wrist.
translations.idiomatic: When a local named Fu Chi seized a pair of greaves from a commoner named Lü Sheng, Luohou had Fu Chi flogged a hundred times and his right wrist cut off.

sentences.zh: 百姓王隴客刺殺民王羌奴、王愈二人，依律罪死而已，洛侯生拔隴客舌，刺其本，并刺胸腹二十餘瘡。

translations.literal: The commoner Wang Longke stabbed and killed the commoners Wang Qiangnu and Wang Yu; by law the crime merited death and nothing more, but Luohou ripped out Longke's tongue while alive, pierced its root, and stabbed his chest and belly with more than twenty wounds.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner named Wang Longke had killed Wang Qiangnu and Wang Yu—an offense that by law deserved only execution. Luohou tore out Longke's tongue while he was still alive, stabbed the stump, and drove more than twenty blades into his chest and belly.

sentences.zh: 隴客不堪苦痛，隨刀戰動。

translations.literal: Longke could not bear the agony and with each cut of the blade writhed.
translations.idiomatic: Longke could not endure the pain and convulsed with every stroke of the blade.

sentences.zh: 乃立四柱磔其手足，命將絕，始斬其首，支解四體，分懸道路。

translations.literal: Then he set up four posts and dismembered his hands and feet on them; when Longke was nearly dead, he finally beheaded him, quartered the four limbs, and hung the parts along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: He then erected four posts and dismembered Longke's limbs upon them; only when life was almost gone did he cut off his head, quarter the body, and hang the pieces along the roads.

sentences.zh: 見之者無不傷楚，闔州驚震，人懷怨憤。

translations.literal: All who saw it were without exception grieved and horrified; the whole province was shaken, and people harbored resentment and rage.
translations.idiomatic: Every witness was appalled; the whole province was shaken, and the people seethed with outrage.

sentences.zh: 百姓王元壽等一時反叛。

translations.literal: The commoners Wang Yuanshou and others rose in revolt all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanshou and other commoners rose in rebellion at once.

sentences.zh: 有司糾劾。

translations.literal: The responsible officials impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities impeached him.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔使者於州刑人處宣告兵民，然後斬洛侯以謝百姓。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered an envoy to proclaim to soldiers and people at the place of execution in the province, then beheaded Luohou to appease the commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sent an envoy to announce the sentence to soldiers and civilians at the execution ground, then had Luohou beheaded to answer the people's grievances.

sentences.zh: 胡泥，代人也。

translations.literal: Hu Ni was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ni was from Dai.

sentences.zh: 歷官至司衞監，賜爵永城侯。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Director of the Palace Guards and was granted the title Marquis of Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Palace Guards and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 泥率勒禁中，不憚豪貴。

translations.literal: Ni led and restrained those within the forbidden quarters, not fearing the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Ni kept order inside the palace precincts and did not shrink from the great and powerful.

sentences.zh: 殿中尚書叔孫侯頭應內直而闕於一時，泥以法繩之。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant Uncle Sun Hutou was due for inner duty but was absent for a time; Ni bound him according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When Palace Attendant Shusun Hutou failed to report for his scheduled inner-palace duty, Ni punished him according to law.

sentences.zh: 侯頭恃寵，遂與口諍。

translations.literal: Hutou relied on favor and thereupon argued with him face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Hutou, trusting in imperial favor, argued back to his face.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而嘉焉，賜泥衣服一襲。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu heard of it and commended him, granting Ni one suit of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu heard of this and commended him, bestowing a full suit of robes.

sentences.zh: 出為幽州刺史，假范陽公。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Governor of You Province, with the provisional title Duke of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of You Province with the provisional title Duke of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 以北平陽尼碩學，遂表薦之。

translations.literal: Because Yang Ni of Beiping was a profound scholar, he memorialized and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Yang Ni of Beiping a distinguished scholar, he memorialized the throne to recommend him.

sentences.zh: 遷平東將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 以暴虐，刑罰酷濫，受納貨賄，徵還戮之。

translations.literal: For cruelty and violence, excessive and abusive penalties, and accepting bribes, he was recalled and executed.
translations.idiomatic: For his brutality, his wanton use of torture, and his acceptance of bribes, he was recalled to the capital and put to death.

sentences.zh: 將就法也，高祖臨太華殿引見，遣侍臣宣詔責之，遂就家賜自盡。

translations.literal: When he was about to face the law, Emperor Gaozu received him at Taihua Hall, sent an attendant to proclaim an edict rebuking him, and then granted him suicide at home.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to be executed, Emperor Gaozu received him in Taihua Hall, had a courtier read out an edict of rebuke, and then allowed him to take his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 李洪之，本名文通，恒農人。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhi, original name Wentong, was a man of Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhi, whose original name was Wentong, was from Hengnong.

sentences.zh: 少為沙門，晚乃還俗。

translations.literal: In youth he was a Buddhist monk; only later did he return to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was a Buddhist monk; only later did he return to secular life.

sentences.zh: 真君中，為狄道護軍，賜爵安陽男。

translations.literal: During the Zhenjun era he was Protector-General of Didao and was granted the title Baron of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenjun reign he served as protector-general of Didao and was enfeoffed as Baron of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 會永昌王仁隨世祖南征，得元后姊妹二人。

translations.literal: It happened that the Prince of Yongchang Ren followed the Shizu emperor on the southern campaign and obtained two sisters of the Yuan empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ren of Yongchang accompanied Emperor Shizu on the southern campaign, he captured two sisters of the future Yuan empress.

sentences.zh: 洪之以宗人潛相餉遺，結為兄弟，遂便如親。

translations.literal: Hongzhi, as a clansman, secretly sent them gifts; they bonded as sworn brothers and soon were as close as kin.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi, claiming kinship, secretly sent them gifts; they swore brotherhood and soon treated one another like family.

sentences.zh: 頗得元后在南兄弟名字，乃改名洪之。

translations.literal: He learned rather fully the names of the Yuan empress's brothers in the south and thereupon changed his name to Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the names of the Yuan empress's brothers in the south, he changed his own name to Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 及仁坐事誅，元后入宮，得幸於高宗，生顯祖。

translations.literal: When Ren was executed for his offense, the Yuan empress entered the palace, won favor from Emperor Gaozong, and bore Emperor Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren was executed for his crimes, the Yuan empress entered the palace, won Emperor Gaozong's favor, and bore Emperor Xianzu.

sentences.zh: 元后臨崩，昭太后問其親，因言洪之為兄。

translations.literal: As the Yuan empress lay dying, Empress Dowager Zhao asked about her kin; she said Hongzhi was her brother.
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed the Yuan empress told Empress Dowager Zhao that Hongzhi was her brother.

sentences.zh: 與相訣經日，具條列南方諸兄珍之等，手以付洪之。

translations.literal: They took leave of one another for days; she fully listed her brothers in the south such as Zhenzhi and handed the list to Hongzhi in her own hand.
translations.idiomatic: They spent days in farewell; she wrote out a full list of her brothers in the south, including Zhenzhi, and handed it to Hongzhi herself.

sentences.zh: 遂號為顯祖親舅。

translations.literal: He was thereby styled Xianzu's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereafter known as Emperor Xianzu's maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 太安中，珍之等兄弟至都，與洪之相見，敍元后平生故事，計長幼為昆季。

translations.literal: In the Tai'an era, Zhenzhi and the other brothers arrived at the capital, met Hongzhi, recounted the Yuan empress's life story, and reckoned seniority to establish themselves as brothers.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tai'an era, Zhenzhi and his brothers reached the capital, met Hongzhi, recounted the Yuan empress's life, and arranged themselves as brothers by age.

sentences.zh: 以外戚為河內太守，進爵任城侯，威儀一同刺史。

translations.literal: As a maternal relative he was made Administrator of Henei, advanced to Marquis of Rencheng, with ceremonial regalia equal to a provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: As a maternal kinsman he was appointed administrator of Henei and advanced to Marquis of Rencheng, with ceremonial honors equal to a provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 河內北連上黨，南接武牢，地險人悍，數為劫害，長吏不能禁。

translations.literal: Henei bordered Shangdang to the north and Wulao to the south; the terrain was rugged and the people fierce, and plunder was frequent — local administrators could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Henei lay between Shangdang to the north and Wulao to the south; the land was rugged and the people fierce, and banditry was constant—local officials could not suppress it.

sentences.zh: 洪之至郡，嚴設科防，募斬賊者便加重賞，勸農務本，盜賊止息。

translations.literal: When Hongzhi reached the commandery he strictly set up regulations and defenses, offered heavy rewards for anyone who slew bandits, urged agriculture and rooted pursuits — banditry ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzhi took office he imposed strict regulations, offered lavish rewards for killing bandits, and urged the people back to farming—banditry soon ceased.

sentences.zh: 誅鋤姦黨，過為酷虐。

translations.literal: He rooted out villainous factions, but went beyond bounds in cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: He rooted out criminal factions, but his methods were excessively cruel.

sentences.zh: 後為懷州刺史，封汲郡公，徵拜內都大官。

translations.literal: Later he was Governor of Huai Province, enfeoffed as Duke of Jijun, and summoned as Grand Official of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: He later became governor of Huai Province, was enfeoffed as Duke of Jijun, and was summoned to serve as Grand Official of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 河西羌胡領部落反叛，顯祖親征，命洪之與侍中、東郡王陸定總統諸軍。

translations.literal: The Qiang and Hu of Hexi led their tribes in rebellion; Xianzu personally campaigned and ordered Hongzhi and the Attendant-in-Ordinary, Prince of Dongjun Lu Ding, to command all armies jointly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang and Hu of Hexi rose in rebellion, Xianzu campaigned in person and ordered Hongzhi and Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Ding, Prince of Dongjun, to command the armies jointly.

sentences.zh: 輿駕至并州，詔洪之為河西都將討山胡。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Bing Province, an edict appointed Hongzhi General of Hexi to subdue the mountain Hu.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession reached Bing Province, an edict appointed Hongzhi general of Hexi to subdue the mountain Hu.

sentences.zh: 皆保險拒戰。

translations.literal: They all held the passes and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: They all held the mountain passes and resisted.

sentences.zh: 洪之築壘於石樓南白鷄原以對之。

translations.literal: Hongzhi built fortifications on the Southern White Cock Plain south of Shilou to face them.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi built a fortified camp on the Southern White Cock Plain south of Shilou to confront them.

sentences.zh: 諸將悉欲進攻，洪之乃開以大信，聽其復業，胡人遂降。

translations.literal: All the generals wished to attack; Hongzhi instead extended great trust and allowed them to resume their livelihoods — the Hu thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: All the generals wanted to attack, but Hongzhi offered them generous terms and let them return to their livelihoods—the Hu then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 顯祖嘉之，遷拜尚書外都大官。

translations.literal: Xianzu commended him and transferred him to Grand Official of the Outer Court in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu commended him and promoted him to Grand Official of the Outer Court in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後為使持節、安南將軍、秦益二州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was Commissioner with extraordinary powers, General Who Pacifies the South, and Governor of Qin and Yi provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as commissioner with extraordinary powers, General Who Pacifies the South, and governor of Qin and Yi provinces.

sentences.zh: 至治，設禁姦之制，有帶刃行者，罪與劫同，輕重品格，各有條章。

translations.literal: In administration he set a system to prohibit misconduct: anyone going about with a blade incurred the same crime as robbery; ranks of severity were each provided with articles.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he instituted strict anti-crime regulations: anyone caught carrying a weapon was punished as a robber, with graded penalties set out in detail.

sentences.zh: 於是大饗州中豪傑長老，示之法制。

translations.literal: He then held a great feast for the province's worthies and elders and showed them the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He then held a great banquet for the province's leading men and elders and displayed the new regulations.

sentences.zh: 乃夜密遣騎分部覆諸要路，有犯禁者，輒捉送州，宣告斬決。

translations.literal: That night he secretly sent horsemen in detachments to patrol the key roads; whoever violated the ban was seized and sent to the province, proclaimed guilty, and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: That night he secretly dispatched cavalry in detachments to patrol the main roads; violators were seized, brought to the provincial capital, and publicly beheaded.

sentences.zh: 其中枉見殺害者百數。

translations.literal: Among them, those wrongly killed numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds among them were innocent victims.

sentences.zh: 赤葩渴郎羌深居山谷，雖相羈縻，王人罕到。

translations.literal: The Chipa Kelang Qiang lived deep in mountain valleys; though nominally under restraint, royal agents rarely reached them.
translations.idiomatic: The Chipa Kelang Qiang lived deep in the mountains; though nominally under imperial control, government agents seldom reached them.

sentences.zh: 洪之芟山為道，廣十餘步，示以軍行之勢，乃興軍臨其境。

translations.literal: Hongzhi cut through mountains for a road more than ten paces wide to display military might, then brought troops to their territory.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi cut a road more than ten paces wide through the mountains to display military might, then marched his army into their territory.

sentences.zh: 山人驚駭。

translations.literal: The mountain people were struck with terror.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain people were terrified.

sentences.zh: 洪之將數十騎至其里閭，撫其妻子，問所疾苦，因資遺之。

translations.literal: Hongzhi took several dozen horsemen to their villages, comforted their wives and children, asked what hardships they suffered, and bestowed gifts upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi rode with several dozen horsemen to their villages, comforted their wives and children, inquired after their hardships, and gave them gifts.

sentences.zh: 眾羌喜悅，求編課調，所入十倍於常。

translations.literal: The Qiang were delighted and asked to be enrolled for taxation; revenue came in ten times the usual amount.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang were delighted and volunteered to register for taxation; revenue from them came to ten times the usual amount.

sentences.zh: 洪之善御戎夷，頗有威惠，而刻害之聲聞於朝野。

translations.literal: Hongzhi was skilled at controlling the barbarians, had considerable authority and favor, yet reports of his cruelty spread through court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi was skilled at managing the frontier peoples and wielded both authority and goodwill, yet reports of his cruelty spread through court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 初，洪之微時，妻張氏助洪之經營資產，自貧至貴，多所補益，有男女幾十人。

translations.literal: Early on, when Hongzhi was still obscure, his wife the Lady Zhang helped him manage property; from poverty to wealth she contributed much — they had several dozen sons and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: In his early days, when Hongzhi was still obscure, his wife Lady Zhang helped him build their fortune; from poverty to wealth she contributed greatly, and they had several dozen children.

sentences.zh: 洪之後得劉氏，劉芳從妹。

translations.literal: Later Hongzhi took the Lady Liu, a cousin of Liu Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hongzhi took Lady Liu, a cousin of Liu Fang.

sentences.zh: 洪之欽重，而疏薄張氏，為兩宅別居，偏厚劉室。

translations.literal: Hongzhi esteemed her highly but treated Lady Zhang coldly; he set up two separate residences, favoring the Liu household.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi favored Liu greatly but treated Lady Zhang coldly; he set up two separate households and lavished favors on the Liu family.

sentences.zh: 由是二妻妬競，互相訟詛，兩宅母子，往來如讎。

translations.literal: Thus the two wives competed in jealousy and sued each other; mothers and sons of both houses came and went like enemies.
translations.idiomatic: The two wives grew jealous and sued one another; mothers and sons in both households treated each other like enemies.

sentences.zh: 及莅西州，以劉自隨。

translations.literal: When he took up office in the western provinces, he brought Liu with him.
translations.idiomatic: When he took up his post in the western provinces, he brought Lady Liu with him.

sentences.zh: 洪之素非廉清，每多受納。

translations.literal: Hongzhi had never been incorrupt; he frequently accepted many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi had never been honest in office and frequently accepted bribes.

sentences.zh: 時高祖始建祿制，法禁嚴峻，司察所聞，無不窮糾。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Gaozu had just established the salary system; laws were stern and inspectors reported everything without fail in thorough investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu had just instituted the salary system; the laws were strict, and inspectors pursued every report to the end.

sentences.zh: 遂鎖洪之赴京。

translations.literal: Hongzhi was shackled and escorted to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi was placed in chains and escorted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖臨太華，庭集羣官，有司奏洪之受贓狼藉，又以酷暴。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu presided at Taihua, assembled officials in the courtyard; the responsible office reported Hongzhi's bribery was rampant and his cruelty extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu held court at Taihua Hall with officials assembled in the courtyard; the authorities reported that Hongzhi's bribery was rampant and his cruelty extreme.

sentences.zh: 高祖親臨數之，以其大臣，聽在家自裁。

translations.literal: The emperor personally rebuked him; as a great minister he was allowed to take his own life at home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him in person; as a senior minister he was permitted to take his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 洪之志性慷慨，多所堪忍，疹疾灸療，艾炷圍將二寸，首足十餘處，一時俱下，而言笑自若，接賓不輟。

translations.literal: Hongzhi's temperament was generous and he bore much; when moxibustion treated his rash, moxa cones nearly two inches around were applied at more than ten places on head and limbs all at once — yet he talked and laughed as usual and received guests without pause.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi was by nature bold and long-suffering; when moxibustion was applied to his rash, cones nearly two inches across were burned at more than ten points on his head and limbs at once—yet he talked and laughed as usual and never stopped receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 及臨自盡，沐浴換衣。

translations.literal: When he faced self-execution he bathed and changed clothes.
translations.idiomatic: When the time came to take his own life, he bathed and changed his clothes.

sentences.zh: 防卒扶持，將出却入，遍遶家庭，如是再三，泣歎良久，乃臥而引藥。

translations.literal: Guards supported him; he started to go out but turned back in, walked round his household three times, wept and sighed a long while, then lay down and took the poison.
translations.idiomatic: Supported by guards, he started to leave but turned back, walked three times around his household, wept and sighed for a long while, then lay down and drank the poison.

sentences.zh: 始洪之託為元后兄，公私自同外戚。

translations.literal: At first Hongzhi had posed as the Yuan empress's brother — everyone privately treated him as a maternal relative.
translations.idiomatic: At first Hongzhi had passed himself off as the Yuan empress's brother, and everyone privately treated him as a maternal kinsman.

sentences.zh: 至此罪後，高祖乃稍對百官辨其誣假，而諸李猶善相視，恩紀如親。

translations.literal: After this crime Emperor Gaozu gradually explained to officials his imposture, yet the various Lis still treated him kindly — bonds of affection like kin.
translations.idiomatic: After his conviction Emperor Gaozu gradually explained to the officials that the kinship was false, yet the Li clan still treated one another warmly, with bonds of affection like true kin.

sentences.zh: 洪之始見元后，計年為兄。

translations.literal: When Hongzhi first met the Yuan empress, by age he counted as her elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzhi first met the Yuan empress, he was older by age and was treated as her elder brother.

sentences.zh: 及珍之等至，洪之以元后素定長幼，其呼拜坐皆如家人。

translations.literal: When Zhenzhi and the others arrived, Hongzhi followed the Yuan empress's settled ranking of seniority; salutations and seating were all as among family.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzhi and his brothers arrived, Hongzhi followed the ranking of seniority the Yuan empress had established; greetings, bows, and seating were all as among family.

sentences.zh: 暮年數延攜之宴飲，醉酣之後，攜之時或言及本末，洪之則起而加敬，笑語自若。

translations.literal: In his later years he often invited Xiezhi to drink; when drunk Xiezhi would sometimes speak of how it all began — Hongzhi would rise and show added respect, chatting and laughing as before.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he often invited Xiezhi to banquets; when drunk, Xiezhi would sometimes speak of how it all began—Hongzhi would rise and show added respect, yet chat and laugh as before.

sentences.zh: 富貴赫弈，當舅戚之家，遂棄宗專附珍之等。

translations.literal: His wealth blazed brilliantly; as head of the maternal clan household he abandoned his own lineage and attached himself solely to Zhenzhi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: His wealth blazed brilliantly; as head of the maternal clan household he abandoned his own lineage and attached himself solely to Zhenzhi and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 後頗存振本屬，而猶不顯然。

translations.literal: Later he somewhat revived ties to his original clan, but not openly.
translations.idiomatic: Later he made some effort to revive ties with his original clan, but not openly.

sentences.zh: 劉氏四子，長子神自有傳。

translations.literal: The Lady Liu had four sons; the eldest Shenyou has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu had four sons; the eldest, Shenyou, has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 高遵，字世禮，勃海蓚人。

translations.literal: Gao Zun, courtesy name Shili, was a man of Su in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zun, courtesy name Shili, was from Su in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 父濟，滄水太守。

translations.literal: His father Ji was Administrator of Cangshui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji served as administrator of Cangshui.

sentences.zh: 遵賤出，兄矯等常欺侮之。

translations.literal: Zun was born of a low-status mother; his elder brothers Qiao and others often bullied him.
translations.idiomatic: Zun was born of a concubine; his elder brothers Qiao and the others often bullied him.

sentences.zh: 及父亡，不令在喪位。

translations.literal: When their father died they would not let him take his place in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When their father died they would not let him take his proper place in the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 遵遂馳赴平城，歸從祖兄中書令允。

translations.literal: Zun galloped to Pingcheng and sought his senior cousin by the paternal line, the Secretariat Director Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Zun galloped to Pingcheng and sought out his father's cousin, Secretariat Director Yun.

sentences.zh: 允乃為遵父舉哀，以遵為喪主，京邑無不弔集，朝貴咸識之。

translations.literal: Yun held mourning for Zun's father, made Zun chief mourner — the capital had none who did not attend; court nobles all came to know him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun held mourning for Zun's father and made Zun chief mourner; the whole capital came to pay respects, and court nobles all came to know him.

sentences.zh: 徐歸奔赴。

translations.literal: He returned slowly to perform the funeral observances.
translations.idiomatic: He returned at leisure to complete the funeral observances.

sentences.zh: 免喪，允為營宦路，得補樂浪王侍郎。

translations.literal: After mourning Yun arranged his official career; he was appointed Attendant of the Prince of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period Yun arranged his official career, and he was appointed attendant to the Prince of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 遵感成益之恩，事允如諸父。

translations.literal: Zun, grateful for Yun's benevolence, served him like an uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for Yun's kindness, Zun served him as he would an uncle.

sentences.zh: 涉歷文史，頗有筆札，進中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He studied literature and history and had considerable skill with the brush; he advanced to Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He studied literature and history and was skilled with the brush; he was promoted to Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 詣長安，刊燕宣王廟碑，進爵安昌子。

translations.literal: He went to Chang'an to carve the temple stele for Prince Xuan of Yan and was advanced to Viscount of Anchang.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Chang'an to carve the temple stele for Prince Xuan of Yan and was advanced to Viscount of Anchang.

sentences.zh: 及新製衣冠，高祖恭薦宗廟，遵形貌莊潔，音氣雄暢，常兼太祝令，跪贊禮事，為俯仰之節，粗合儀矩。

translations.literal: When new caps and robes were made and Emperor Gaozu reverently offered at the ancestral temple, Zun's bearing was dignified and his voice resonant; he regularly doubled as Director of Sacrifices, kneeling to intone the rites — the motions of bowing and rising roughly fit protocol.
translations.idiomatic: When new caps and robes were made and Emperor Gaozu offered sacrifice at the ancestral temple, Zun's bearing was dignified and his voice resonant; he regularly served as Director of Sacrifices, kneeling to intone the rites—the motions of bowing and rising roughly conformed to ritual.

sentences.zh: 由是高祖識待之。

translations.literal: Thereby Emperor Gaozu came to notice and favor him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby Emperor Gaozu came to notice and favor him.

sentences.zh: 後與游明根、高閭、李沖入議律令，親對御坐，時有陳奏。

translations.literal: Later he joined You Minggen, Gao Lü, and Li Chong in deliberating on statutes; facing the imperial seat he sometimes presented memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined You Minggen, Gao Lü, and Li Chong in deliberating on statutes; facing the imperial throne he sometimes presented memorials.

sentences.zh: 以積年之勞，賜粟帛牛馬。

translations.literal: For accumulated years of service he was given grain, silk, cattle, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: For years of accumulated service he was rewarded with grain, silk, cattle, and horses.

sentences.zh: 出為立忠將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General Who Establishes Loyalty and Governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Establishes Loyalty and governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 建節歷本州，宗鄉改觀，而矯等彌妬毀之。

translations.literal: Bearing the staff of authority he governed his home province; clansmen changed their view of him, while Qiao and the others hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing the staff of authority he governed his home province; clansmen changed their view of him, while Qiao and his brothers hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 遵性不廉清，在中書時，每假歸山東，必借備騾馬，將從百餘。

translations.literal: Zun's nature was not incorrupt; while in the Secretariat, each time he took leave to return to Shandong he had to borrow pack mules and horses with more than a hundred attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Zun was not honest in office; while at the Secretariat, each time he took leave to return to Shandong he borrowed pack mules and horses and traveled with more than a hundred attendants.

sentences.zh: 屯逼民家求絲縑，不滿意則詬罵不去，強相徵求。

translations.literal: He camped and pressed upon commoners' homes demanding silk; if unsatisfied he cursed and would not leave, forcibly exacting goods.
translations.idiomatic: He camped at commoners' homes demanding silk; if unsatisfied he cursed and refused to leave, forcibly exacting goods.

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，縑布千數。

translations.literal: Within a month or so, silk and cloth numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month or so he accumulated thousands of bolts of silk and cloth.

sentences.zh: 邦邑苦之。

translations.literal: The commandery and districts suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: The whole region suffered under him.

sentences.zh: 遵既臨州，本意未弭，選召僚吏，多所取納。

translations.literal: Once Zun took up the governorship his original intent was not quelled; he selected and summoned subordinate officials and took many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zun took office his rapacity did not abate; he summoned subordinates and extorted bribes from many of them.

sentences.zh: 又其妻明氏家在齊州，母弟舅甥共相憑屬，爭求貨利，嚴暴非理，殺害甚多。

translations.literal: Moreover his wife the Lady Ming's family was in Qi Province; mother, younger brothers, uncles, and nephews relied on one another, vied for profit, were stern and violent beyond reason, and killed many.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Ming's family lived in Qi Province; her mother, brothers, uncles, and nephews relied on one another to scramble for profit, acting with brutal violence beyond reason and killing many people.

sentences.zh: 貪酷之響，帝頗聞之。

translations.literal: Reports of his greed and cruelty reached the emperor rather fully.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard considerable reports of his greed and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 及車駕幸鄴，遵自州來朝，會有赦宥。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Ye, Zun came from his province to court — it happened there was a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Ye, Zun came from his province to pay court, and a general amnesty happened to be declared.

sentences.zh: 遵臨還州，請辭帝於行宮，引見誚讓之。

translations.literal: As Zun was about to return to his province he requested leave of the emperor at the traveling palace; he was summoned and rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: As Zun was about to return to his province he took leave of the emperor at the traveling palace and was summoned and rebuked.

sentences.zh: 遵自陳無負，帝厲聲曰：「若無遷都赦，必無高遵矣！

translations.literal: Zun declared himself innocent; the emperor said in a harsh voice: "If not for the amnesty on the capital's move, there would certainly be no Gao Zun!
translations.idiomatic: Zun protested his innocence. The emperor said sharply, "If not for the amnesty proclaimed when the capital was moved, Gao Zun would certainly be dead!

sentences.zh: 又卿非惟貪惏，又虐於刑法，謂何如濟陰王，猶不免於法。

translations.literal: Moreover you are not only greedy, you are also cruel in penal law — what of the Prince of Jiyin? He still did not escape the law.
translations.idiomatic: And you are not only greedy but brutal in your use of the law—consider the Prince of Jiyin: even he could not escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 卿何人，而為此行！

translations.literal: Who are you, to act in this way!
translations.idiomatic: Who do you think you are, to behave like this!

sentences.zh: 自今宜自謹約。

translations.literal: From now on you should restrain yourself.
translations.idiomatic: From now on you must restrain yourself.

sentences.zh: 」還州，仍不悛革。

translations.literal: " He returned to his province but still did not repent and reform.
translations.idiomatic: " Zun returned to his province but still did not reform.

sentences.zh: 齊州人孟僧振至洛訟遵。

translations.literal: A man of Qi Province, Meng Zhen, went to Luoyang to sue Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhen of Qi Province went to Luoyang to bring suit against Zun.

sentences.zh: 詔廷尉少卿劉述窮鞫，皆如所訴。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Vice Director of the Court of Justice Liu Shu to investigate thoroughly; everything was as alleged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Vice Director of the Court of Justice Liu Shu to investigate thoroughly; the charges were all substantiated.

sentences.zh: 先是，沙門道登過遵，遵以道登荷寵於高祖，多奉以貨，深託仗之。

translations.literal: Earlier the monk Daodeng had visited Zun; Zun, because Daodeng enjoyed favor with Emperor Gaozu, presented him with many goods and deeply relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the monk Daodeng had visited Zun; because Daodeng enjoyed Emperor Gaozu's favor, Zun gave him many gifts and placed great trust in him.

sentences.zh: 道登屢因言次申啟救遵，帝不省納，遂詔述賜遵死。

translations.literal: Daodeng repeatedly took occasion in conversation to plead to save Zun; the emperor did not heed it, and thereupon ordered Liu Shu to grant Zun death.
translations.idiomatic: Daodeng repeatedly interceded for Zun when he had the emperor's ear, but the emperor would not listen and ordered Liu Shu to sentence Zun to death.

sentences.zh: 時遵子元榮詣洛訟冤，猶恃道登，不時還赴。

translations.literal: At that time Zun's son Yuanrong went to Luoyang to plead injustice; still relying on Daodeng, he did not return in time.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's son Yuanrong went to Luoyang to plead his father's case; still trusting in Daodeng, he did not return home in time.

sentences.zh: 道登知事決，方乃遣之。

translations.literal: When Daodeng knew the matter was settled, only then did he send him back.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Daodeng knew the sentence was final did he send Yuanrong home.

sentences.zh: 遵恨其妻，不與訣，別處沐浴，引椒而死。

translations.literal: Zun hated his wife and would not take leave of her; he bathed elsewhere and drank pepper poison to die.
translations.idiomatic: Zun hated his wife and refused to bid her farewell; he bathed in a separate room and drank pepper poison to die.

sentences.zh: 元榮，學尚有文才，長於几案。

translations.literal: Yuanrong was learned and had literary talent, skilled at desk work.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanrong was learned and talented with the pen, skilled at administrative work.

sentences.zh: 位兼尚書右丞，為西道行臺，至高平鎮，遇城翻被害。

translations.literal: He held the concurrent post of Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, served as Western Route Commissioner, reached Gaoping garrison, and was killed when the city rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and as Western Route Commissioner; when he reached Gaoping garrison the city rose in revolt and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 遵弟次文，雖無位官而貲產巨萬。

translations.literal: Zun's younger brother Ciwen, though without an official post, had property worth tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's younger brother Ciwen held no office but possessed wealth in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 遵每責其財，又結憾於遵，吉凶不相往反。

translations.literal: Zun constantly demanded his wealth; Ciwen also bore resentment toward Zun — in fortune or misfortune they did not visit one another.
translations.idiomatic: Zun constantly demanded money from him; Ciwen bore a grudge against Zun as well, and they never visited one another in good times or bad.

sentences.zh: 時論責之。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion censured him.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion censured him for this.

sentences.zh: 張赦提，中山安喜人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Sheti was a man of Anxi in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheti was from Anxi in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 性雄武，有規畫。

translations.literal: His nature was bold and martial, with strategic planning.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and martial by nature and skilled in planning.

sentences.zh: 初為虎賁中郎。

translations.literal: At first he was a Tiger Guard Central Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Tiger Guard Central Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 時京畿盜魁自稱豹子、虎子，並善弓馬，遂領逃連及諸畜牧者，[2]各為部帥，於靈丘、雁門間聚為劫害。

translations.literal: At that time bandit chiefs of the capital region called themselves Leopard Son and Tiger Son; both were skilled in bow and horse, then led fugitives and various herders, each as a unit commander, gathering between Lingqiu and Yanmen to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the chief bandits of the capital region called themselves Leopard Son and Tiger Son; both were skilled archers and horsemen. They gathered fugitives and herders as their followers and plundered the region between Lingqiu and Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 至乃斬人首，射其口，刺人臍，引腸遶樹而共射之，以為戲笑。

translations.literal: They even beheaded people, shot their mouths, stabbed people's navels, drew out intestines and wound them around trees to shoot at together, taking it as sport and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: They would behead victims, shoot arrows into their mouths, stab their navels, draw out their intestines and wind them around trees for target practice—all as sport.

sentences.zh: 其為暴酷如此。

translations.literal: Their violence and cruelty were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Their cruelty was of this sort.

sentences.zh: 軍騎掩㨞，久弗能獲，行者患焉。

translations.literal: Cavalry raided and searched, but for long could not capture them; travelers suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Government cavalry hunted them for a long time without success, and travelers lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 赦提設防遏追窮之計，宰司善之，以赦提為逐賊軍將。

translations.literal: Sheti devised plans to block, pursue, and root them out; the chief ministers approved and made Sheti General for Pursuing Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Sheti devised plans to block and pursue the bandits to the end; the chief ministers approved and appointed him general for pursuing bandits.

sentences.zh: 乃求驍勇追之，未幾而獲虎子、豹子及其黨與。

translations.literal: He then sought fierce warriors to pursue them; before long he captured Tiger Son, Leopard Son, and their followers.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited fierce warriors to pursue them and soon captured Tiger Son, Leopard Son, and their followers.

sentences.zh: 盡送京師，斬於闕下，自是清靜。

translations.literal: All were sent to the capital and beheaded below the palace gate; from then on there was peace.
translations.idiomatic: They were all sent to the capital and beheaded at the palace gate; the region was quiet thereafter.

sentences.zh: 其靈丘羅思祖宗門豪溢，家處隘險，多止亡命，與之為劫。

translations.literal: At Lingqiu the Luo Sizu clan's lineage was powerful and overflowing; their home lay in narrow and dangerous terrain, and many fugitives stayed with them to plunder together.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingqiu the Luo Sizu clan was powerful; their estate lay in rugged terrain where many fugitives took refuge and joined them in banditry.

sentences.zh: 顯祖怒之，孥戮其家。

translations.literal: Xianzu was enraged and exterminated their entire family.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu was enraged and exterminated the entire clan.

sentences.zh: 而思祖家黨，相率寇盜。

translations.literal: But Sizu's kinsmen and followers banded together in raiding and robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Sizu's kinsmen and followers then banded together in raids.

sentences.zh: 赦提應募求捕逐，乃以赦提為游徼軍將，前後禽獲，殺之略盡。

translations.literal: Sheti volunteered to seek and capture them; he was made Patrol General, and before and after captured them and killed nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Sheti volunteered to hunt them down and was appointed Patrol General; he captured and killed nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 因而濫有屠害，尤為忍酷。

translations.literal: Thereby he indiscriminately slaughtered many, especially cruel and hard to bear.
translations.idiomatic: In the process he indiscriminately slaughtered many people, showing extreme cruelty.

sentences.zh: 既資前稱，又藉此功，除冠軍將軍、幽州刺史，假安喜侯。

translations.literal: Relying on his earlier reputation and also on this merit, he was appointed General Who Crowns the Army and Governor of You Province, with the provisional title Marquis of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Building on his earlier reputation and this new success, he was appointed General Who Crowns the Army and governor of You Province, with the provisional title Marquis of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 赦提克己厲約，遂有清稱。

translations.literal: Sheti restrained himself and was strict in discipline, and thereby gained a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Sheti disciplined himself strictly and gained a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 後頗縱妻段氏，多有受納，令僧尼因事通請，貪虐流聞。

translations.literal: Later he rather indulged his wife the Lady Duan; there were many bribes accepted; he had monks and nuns use affairs to gain access and plead — reports of greed and cruelty spread.
translations.idiomatic: Later he indulged his wife Lady Duan, who accepted many bribes and had monks and nuns intercede on her behalf; reports of their greed and cruelty spread widely.

sentences.zh: 中散李真香出使幽州，採訪牧守政績。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Li Zhenxiang was sent on mission to You Province to investigate the achievements of governors and administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Li Zhenxiang was dispatched to You Province to investigate the conduct of local officials.

sentences.zh: 真香驗案其罪，赦提懼死欲逃。

translations.literal: Zhenxiang verified and prosecuted his crimes; Sheti feared death and wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenxiang verified his crimes; Sheti, fearing execution, planned to flee.

sentences.zh: 其妻姑為太尉、東陽王丕妻，恃丕親貴，自許詣丕申訴求助，謂赦提曰：「當為訴理，幸得申雪，願且寬憂，不為異計。

translations.literal: His wife's aunt was wife of the Grand Commandant, Prince of Dongyang Pi; relying on Pi's kinship and nobility, she promised to go to Pi to plead and seek help, telling Sheti: "I will plead your case; we may yet clear your name — for now ease your worry and do not take other measures."
translations.idiomatic: His wife's aunt was the wife of Grand Commandant Pi, Prince of Dongyang; relying on Pi's rank and influence, she promised to appeal to him and told Sheti, "I will plead your case; we may yet clear your name—for now set your mind at ease and do nothing rash."

sentences.zh: 」赦提以此差自解慰。

translations.literal: " Sheti was somewhat relieved and consoled by this.
translations.idiomatic: " Sheti was somewhat reassured by this.

sentences.zh: 段乃陳列真香昔嘗因假而過幽州，知赦提有好牛，從索不果。

translations.literal: Duan then set forth that Zhenxiang had once passed through You Province on leave, knew Sheti had a fine ox, and sought it from him without success.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Duan then argued that Zhenxiang had once passed through You Province on leave, knew Sheti owned a fine ox, had asked for it and been refused.

sentences.zh: 今臺使心協前事，[3]故威逼部下，拷楚過極，橫以無辜，證成誣罪。

translations.literal: Now the imperial envoy's heart agreed with the earlier affair; therefore he intimidated subordinates, torture exceeded all bounds, and on the innocent he forced false evidence to fabricate a trumped-up crime.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial envoy was acting on that old grudge, intimidating Sheti's subordinates, torturing them beyond all bounds, and fabricating charges against the innocent.

sentences.zh: 執事恐有不盡，使駕部令趙秦州重往究訊。

translations.literal: The responsible officials feared the matter was not complete and sent Chariot Department Director Zhao of Qin Province to go again and investigate thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities, fearing the investigation was incomplete, sent Chariot Department Director Zhao of Qin Province to reinvestigate.

sentences.zh: 事伏如前，處赦提大辟。

translations.literal: The matter was established as before; Sheti was sentenced to the great penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The charges were confirmed as before, and Sheti was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔賜死於第。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered by edict that he be granted death at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu ordered him granted death at his residence.

sentences.zh: 將就盡，召妻而責之曰：「貪濁穢吾者卿也，又安吾而不得免禍，九泉之下當為仇讎矣。」

translations.literal: As he was about to die he summoned his wife and rebuked her: "It was you who by greed and corruption defiled me; you also comforted me yet could not spare me from disaster — in the nine springs below we shall be enemies."
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to die he summoned his wife and rebuked her: "Your greed and corruption have ruined me; you comforted me yet could not save me from this fate—in the world below we shall be enemies."

sentences.zh: 又有華山太守趙霸，酷暴非理。

translations.literal: There was also Administrator of Huashan Zhao Ba, cruel and violent beyond reason.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhao Ba, administrator of Huashan, who was brutal beyond all reason.

sentences.zh: 大使崔光奏霸云：「不遵憲度，威虐任情，至乃手擊吏人，僚屬奔走。

translations.literal: Commissioner Cui Guang memorialized against Ba saying: "He does not observe the statutes, acts with fierce cruelty as he pleases, even to the point of striking clerks and attendants with his own hands — subordinates flee in panic."
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Cui Guang memorialized against Ba: "He disregards the law, acts with arbitrary cruelty, even striking clerks with his own hands while his subordinates flee in terror."

sentences.zh: 不可以君人字下，納之軌物，輒禁止在州。

translations.literal: He cannot be allowed to rule over people and be brought within the norms — he is forthwith forbidden to remain in the province."
translations.idiomatic: He is unfit to govern people or be held to proper standards—he is forthwith barred from remaining in the province."

sentences.zh: 」詔免所居官。

translations.literal: " An edict removed him from the office he held.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict stripped him of his office.

sentences.zh: 羊祉，字靈祐，太山鉅平人，晉太僕卿琇之六世孫也。

translations.literal: Yang Zhi, courtesy name Lingyou, was a man of Juping in Taishan, sixth-generation descendant of Jin Minister of Coachmen Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhi, courtesy name Lingyou, was from Juping in Taishan, a sixth-generation descendant of Jin Minister of Coachmen Yang Xiu.

sentences.zh: 父規之，宋任城令。

translations.literal: His father Guizhi was Magistrate of Rencheng under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guizhi served as magistrate of Rencheng under the Song.

sentences.zh: 世祖南討至鄒山，規之與魯郡太守崔邪利及其屬縣徐通、愛猛之等俱降，賜爵鉅平子，拜雁門太守。

translations.literal: When the Shizu emperor campaigned south to Zou Mountain, Guizhi together with Administrator of Lu Commandery Cui Xieli and subordinates of his counties Xu Tong, Ai Mengzhi, and others all surrendered; he was granted the title Viscount of Juping and appointed Administrator of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu marched south to Zou Mountain, Guizhi surrendered together with Cui Xieli, administrator of Lu Commandery, and officials of his subordinate counties including Xu Tong and Ai Mengzhi; he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Juping and appointed administrator of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 祉性剛愎，好刑名，為司空令輔國長史，[4]襲爵鉅平子。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was stubborn and willful; he favored penal law; he was Chief Clerk Assisting the State under the Minister of Works and inherited the title Viscount of Juping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was stubborn and willful by nature and fond of penal law; he served as Chief Clerk Assisting the State under the Minister of Works and inherited the title Viscount of Juping.

sentences.zh: 侵盜公資，私營居宅，有司案之抵死，高祖特恕遠徙。

translations.literal: He embezzled public funds and built a private residence; the responsible office prosecuted him for death, but Emperor Gaozu specially pardoned him and exiled him far away.
translations.idiomatic: He embezzled public funds and built a private residence; the authorities prosecuted him for a capital offense, but Emperor Gaozu specially pardoned him and exiled him to a distant place.

sentences.zh: 後還。

translations.literal: Later he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned.

sentences.zh: 景明初，為將作都將，加左軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingming era he was Director of Palace Construction and additionally Left Army General.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingming era he served as Director of Palace Construction and was additionally appointed Left Army General.

sentences.zh: 四年，持節為梁州軍司，討叛氐。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he held the staff of authority as Military Commissioner of Liang Province and subdued rebellious Di.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he held the staff of authority as military commissioner of Liang Province and campaigned against rebellious Di tribes.

sentences.zh: 正始二年，王師伐蜀，以祉假節、龍驤將軍、益州刺史，出劍閣而還。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengshi the royal army attacked Shu; Zhi was given provisional staff, made General of the Dragon Cavalry and Governor of Yi Province, advanced through Jian'ge Pass and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengshi the imperial army attacked Shu; Zhi was given provisional authority as General of the Dragon Cavalry and governor of Yi Province, advanced through Jian'ge Pass, and returned.

sentences.zh: 又以本將軍為秦梁二州刺史，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He was again made with his former rank General of Qin and Liang provinces, and additionally General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed governor of Qin and Liang provinces with his former rank, and additionally made General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 天性酷忍，又不清潔。

translations.literal: By nature he was cruel and hard to bear, and also not clean in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was cruel and dishonest in office.

sentences.zh: 坐掠人為奴婢，為御史中尉王顯所彈免。

translations.literal: He was convicted of seizing people as slaves and bondmaids; Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian impeached him and he was removed.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted of seizing people as slaves; Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 高肇南征，祉復被起為光祿大夫、假平南將軍，持節領步騎三萬先驅趣涪。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhao campaigned south, Zhi was again summoned as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and provisional General Who Pacifies the South, holding the staff of authority leading thirty thousand infantry and cavalry as vanguard hurrying to Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhao campaigned south, Zhi was recalled as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and provisional General Who Pacifies the South, leading thirty thousand infantry and cavalry as vanguard toward Fu.

sentences.zh: 未至，世宗崩，班師。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Emperor Shizong died and the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, Emperor Shizong died and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夜中引軍，山有二徑，軍人迷而失路。

translations.literal: He led the army by night; the mountain had two paths and the soldiers lost their way in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: He led the army by night; the mountain had two paths and the soldiers lost their way.

sentences.zh: 祉便斬隊副楊明達，梟首路側。

translations.literal: Zhi immediately beheaded squad deputy Yang Mingda and displayed his head by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi immediately beheaded squad deputy Yang Mingda and displayed his head by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 為中尉元昭所劾，會赦免。

translations.literal: He was impeached by Commandant Yuan Zhao; it happened there was an amnesty and he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Yuan Zhao impeached him, but he was pardoned in a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 後加平北將軍，未拜而卒。

translations.literal: Later he was made General Who Pacifies the North but died before assuming the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed General Who Pacifies the North but died before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 贈安東將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was given the title General Who Pacifies the East and governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿元端、博士劉臺龍議諡曰：「祉志存埋輪，不避強禦。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Yuan Duan and Erudite Liu Tailong deliberated on the posthumous title, saying: "Zhi's will was set on burying the wheel — he did not avoid the powerful and overbearing."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Yuan Duan and Erudite Liu Tailong proposed the posthumous title, saying, "Zhi was determined to curb abuse of power and did not shrink from the mighty."

sentences.zh: 及贊戎律，熊武斯裁，仗節撫藩，邊夷識德，化沾殊類，襁負懷仁。

translations.literal: When he assisted military law, his bear-like martial prowess was displayed; bearing the staff he pacified the frontier; border barbarians knew his virtue; his transforming influence reached diverse peoples; infants in swaddling clothes cherished his benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: In military affairs he showed fierce martial prowess; bearing the imperial staff he governed the frontier, where border peoples recognized his virtue; his civilizing influence reached all peoples, and even infants in arms felt his benevolence."

sentences.zh: 謹依諡法，布德行剛曰『景』，宜諡為景。

translations.literal: Respectfully according to the posthumous-title law, 'spreading virtue with a firm nature' is Jing — the appropriate posthumous title is Jing."
translations.idiomatic: According to the posthumous-title law, 'spreading virtue with a firm nature' yields Jing—the appropriate posthumous title is Jing."

sentences.zh: 」侍中侯剛、給事黃門侍郎元纂等駁曰：「臣聞惟名與器，弗可妄假，定諡準行，必當其迹。

translations.literal: " Attendant-in-Ordinary Hou Gang, Attendant of the Yellow Gate Yuan Zuan, and others objected: "Your servant has heard that names and insignia must not be lightly bestowed; fixing a posthumous title according to conduct must match the deeds."
translations.idiomatic: " Attendant-in-Ordinary Hou Gang, Attendant of the Yellow Gate Yuan Zuan, and others objected: "We have heard that titles and honors must not be lightly bestowed; a posthumous name must match the man's actual conduct."

sentences.zh: 案祉志性急酷，所在過威，布德罕聞，暴聲屢發。

translations.literal: Examining Zhi, his will and nature were harsh and cruel; wherever he served he exceeded in severity; spreading virtue was rarely heard; reports of violence arose repeatedly."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's nature was harsh and cruel; wherever he served he ruled with excessive severity; spreading virtue was rarely heard of, while reports of his violence arose repeatedly."

sentences.zh: 而禮官虛述，諡之為『景』，非直失於一人，實毀朝則。

translations.literal: Yet the ritual officials described him falsely and gave the title Jing — this is not merely a loss regarding one man, it truly damages the court's standards."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ritual officials have described him falsely and proposed Jing—not merely wrong for one man, but a true damage to the court's standards."

sentences.zh: 請還付外準行，更量虛實。

translations.literal: We request that it be returned to the outer offices to judge according to conduct and reweigh truth and falsehood."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the matter be returned to the outer offices to judge according to his actual conduct."

sentences.zh: 」靈太后令曰：「依駁更議。

translations.literal: " Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "Follow the objection and deliberate again."
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Dowager Ling ordered, "Accept the objection and deliberate again."

sentences.zh: 」元端、臺龍上言：「竊惟諡者行之迹，狀者迹之稱。

translations.literal: " Yuan Duan and Tailong submitted: "Your servant considers that the posthumous title is the trace of conduct, and the description is the name for the trace."
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Duan and Tailong submitted, "We consider that the posthumous title records a man's conduct, and the description is the name given to that record."

sentences.zh: 然尚書銓衡是司，釐品庶物，若狀與跡乖，應抑而不受，錄其實狀，然後下寺，依諡法準狀科上。

translations.literal: Yet the Secretariat is charged with weighing and balancing, ordering all things — if the description and the trace diverge, it should be suppressed and not accepted; record the true description, then send down to the temple offices to fix the title according to the posthumous law and submit by category."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat is charged with evaluating officials; if the description and the conduct diverge, it should be rejected, the true record entered, and only then sent to the temple offices to fix the title according to law."

sentences.zh: 豈有捨其行迹，外有所求，去狀去稱，將何所準？

translations.literal: How can one abandon his conduct and trace, seek something outside, remove description and name — what will serve as standard?"
translations.idiomatic: How can one abandon his actual conduct, seek some external standard, and discard both description and title—what would then serve as the basis?"

sentences.zh: 檢祉以母老辭藩，乃降手詔云：『卿綏撫有年，聲實兼著，安邊寧境，實稱朝望。

translations.literal: Examining Zhi: when he declined the frontier post because his mother was old, an imperial handwritten edict was issued saying: 'You have pacified and comforted for years; reputation and achievement are both manifest; securing the border and settling the territory truly matches the court's hopes.'
translations.idiomatic: Consider that when Zhi declined a frontier post because his mother was elderly, the emperor issued a handwritten edict saying, 'You have governed for years with reputation and achievement alike; securing the border truly meets the court's expectations.'

sentences.zh: 』及其歿也，又加顯贈，言祉誠著累朝，效彰內外，作牧岷區，字萌之績驟聞。

translations.literal: ' When he died, there was again a splendid posthumous grant, saying Zhi's sincerity was manifest through successive reigns, achievements shown within and without; as shepherd of the Min region, his civilizing achievements for the young were suddenly heard.
translations.idiomatic: ' When he died, the court granted him splendid posthumous honors, declaring that Zhi's loyalty had been manifest through successive reigns, his achievements known within and without; as governor of the Min region, his civilizing achievements were widely reported.

sentences.zh: 詔冊褒美，無替倫望。

translations.literal: Edicts and patent letters praised him — none could replace his standing.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial edicts and patent letters praised him without stint.

sentences.zh: 然君子使人器之義，無求備德。

translations.literal: Yet the gentleman uses people for their strengths — he does not demand complete virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the gentleman uses a man for his strengths and does not demand perfection in every virtue.

sentences.zh: 有數德優劣不同，剛而能克，亦為德焉。

translations.literal: When several virtues differ in excellence and inferiority, firmness that can overcome is also a virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When virtues differ in degree, firmness that can overcome obstacles is itself a virtue.

sentences.zh: 謹依諡法，布德行剛曰『景』，謂前議為允。

translations.literal: Respectfully according to the posthumous-title law, 'spreading virtue with a firm nature' is Jing — the former proposal is deemed fitting."
translations.idiomatic: According to the posthumous-title law, 'spreading virtue with a firm nature' yields Jing—we hold the former proposal to be fitting."

sentences.zh: 」司徒右長史張烈、主簿李瑒刺稱：「案祉歷宦累朝，當官之稱。

translations.literal: " Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of State Zhang Lie and Registrar Li Chang submitted: "Examining Zhi, he served through successive reigns with a reputation fitting to his office."
translations.idiomatic: " Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of State Zhang Lie and Registrar Li Chang submitted, "Zhi served through successive reigns with a reputation fitting to his offices."

sentences.zh: 委捍西南，邊隅靖遏。

translations.literal: Entrusted to defend the southwest, the border corners were pacified and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with defending the southwest, he pacified the frontier regions.

sentences.zh: 準行易名，奬誡攸在。

translations.literal: According to conduct to change the name — reward and admonition lie therein.
translations.idiomatic: To judge conduct and fix a name is to offer reward and warning alike.

sentences.zh: 竊謂無虧體例。

translations.literal: Your servant considers there is no detriment to precedent."
translations.idiomatic: We consider that this does no injury to precedent."

sentences.zh: 」尚書李韶又述奏以府寺為允，靈太后可其奏。

translations.literal: " Director of the Secretariat Li Shao again memorialized that the government offices' view was fitting; Empress Dowager Ling approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " Director of the Secretariat Li Shao again memorialized that the government offices' view was fitting; Empress Dowager Ling approved it.

sentences.zh: 祉自當官，不憚強禦，朝廷以為剛斷，時有檢覆，每令出使。

translations.literal: From the time Zhi held office he did not fear the powerful and overbearing; the court regarded him as firm and decisive; there were periodic inspections and he was often sent on missions.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his career Zhi did not fear the powerful; the court regarded him as firm and decisive, and he was often sent on inspection missions.

sentences.zh: 好慕名利，頗為深文，所經之處，人號天狗下。

translations.literal: He loved and sought fame and profit, was rather severe in legal wording; wherever he passed, people called it 'the celestial dog descending.'
translations.idiomatic: He craved fame and profit and was harsh in his application of the law; wherever he went, people said 'the celestial dog has descended.'

sentences.zh: 及出將臨州，並無恩潤，兵民患其嚴虐焉。

translations.literal: When he went out as general and took up a province, there was no benevolent grace at all — soldiers and people suffered under his severity and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: When he served as general and governor he showed no benevolence at all—soldiers and civilians alike suffered under his severity.

sentences.zh: 崔暹，字元欽，本云清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Xian, courtesy name Yuanqin, was originally said to be from Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xian, courtesy name Yuanqin, was said to be originally from Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 世家于滎陽、潁川之間。

translations.literal: His clan had long been established between Xingyang and Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been established between Xingyang and Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 性猛酷，少仁恕，姦猾好利，能事勢家。

translations.literal: His nature was fierce and cruel, with little kindness and forbearance; he was treacherous, cunning, and fond of profit, able to serve powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce and cruel by nature, showing little mercy; he was treacherous and greedy, and skilled at currying favor with the powerful.

sentences.zh: 初以秀才累遷南兗州刺史，盜用官瓦，贓污狼藉，為御史中尉李平所糾，免官。

translations.literal: At first as a xiucai he rose through posts to Governor of Southern Yan Province; he stole and used official tiles, his bribery was rampant, and Censor-in-Chief Li Ping impeached him — he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a xiucai, he rose to governor of Southern Yan Province; he misappropriated official tiles, his corruption was rampant, and Censor-in-Chief Li Ping impeached him and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 後行豫州事，尋即真。

translations.literal: Later he acted as administrator of Yu Province and soon received the full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He later acted as administrator of Yu Province and soon received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 坐遣子析戶，分隸三縣，廣占田宅，藏匿官奴，障吝陂葦，侵盜公私，為御史中尉王顯所彈，免官。

translations.literal: He was convicted of sending his son to split the household and register members under three counties, broadly seizing fields and residences, hiding government slaves, monopolizing pond reeds, and encroaching on public and private property — Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian impeached him and he was removed.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted of having his son split the household to register members under three counties, seizing vast tracts of land, hiding government slaves, monopolizing pond reeds, and encroaching on public and private property; Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 後累遷平北將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he rose through posts to General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 貪暴安忍，民庶患之。

translations.literal: Greedy, violent, and calmly cruel, the common people suffered from him.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy, brutal, and utterly pitiless, he was a scourge to the common people.

sentences.zh: 嘗出獵州北，單騎至於民村。

translations.literal: Once when hunting north of the province he rode alone to a commoners' village.
translations.idiomatic: Once while hunting north of the province he rode alone into a village.

sentences.zh: 井有汲水婦人，暹令飲馬，因問曰：「崔瀛州何如？

translations.literal: At a well was a woman drawing water; Xian had her water his horse and then asked: "How is Cui, Governor of Ying?"
translations.idiomatic: At a well a woman was drawing water; Xian had her water his horse and asked, "What do you think of Governor Cui of Ying Province?"

sentences.zh: 」婦人不知其暹也，答曰：「百姓何罪，得如此癩兒刺史！

translations.literal: " The woman did not know it was Xian and answered: "What crime have the common people committed, to get such a leper-son of a governor!"
translations.idiomatic: " Not knowing it was Xian himself, the woman replied, "What have the people done to deserve such a leprous wretch as governor!"

sentences.zh: 」暹默然而去。

translations.literal: " Xian departed in silence.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian departed without a word.

sentences.zh: 以不稱職被解還京。

translations.literal: For incompetence in office he was dismissed and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed for incompetence, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 武川鎮反，詔暹為都督，隸大都督李崇討之。

translations.literal: When Wuchuan Garrison rebelled, an edict made Xian Commander, subordinate to Grand Commander Li Chong to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchuan Garrison rebelled, an edict appointed Xian commander under Grand Commander Li Chong to suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 違崇節度，為賊所敗，單騎潛還。

translations.literal: He violated Chong's command, was defeated by the rebels, and slipped back alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: He disobeyed Chong's orders, was defeated by the rebels, and fled back alone.

sentences.zh: 禁於廷尉。

translations.literal: He was detained by the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned by the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 以女妓園田貨元叉，獲免。

translations.literal: He bribed Yuan Cha with female entertainers, gardens, and fields, and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He bribed Yuan Cha with female entertainers, gardens, and fields and obtained his release.

sentences.zh: 建義初遇害於河陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒公、冀州刺史，追封武津縣公。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Duke of the Secretariat and Governor of Ji Province, and enfeoffed retroactively as Duke of Wujin County.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was given the title Duke of the Secretariat and governor of Ji Province, and retroactively enfeoffed as Duke of Wujin County.

sentences.zh: 子瓚，字紹珍。

translations.literal: His son Zan, courtesy name Shaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zan, courtesy name Shaozhen.

sentences.zh: 位兼尚書左丞，卒。

translations.literal: He held the concurrent post of Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and died in office.

sentences.zh: 瓚妻，莊帝妹也，後封襄城長公主，故特贈瓚冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Zan's wife was a sister of Emperor Zhuang; later she was enfeoffed as Princess of Xiangcheng, and therefore Zan was specially granted posthumously as Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's wife was a sister of Emperor Zhuang; she was later enfeoffed as Princess of Xiangcheng, and Zan was therefore specially granted posthumously the title governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 子茂，字祖昂，襲祖爵。

translations.literal: His son Mao, courtesy name Zu'ang, inherited his grandfather's title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mao, courtesy name Zu'ang, inherited his grandfather's title.

sentences.zh: 酈道元，字善長，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Daoyuan, courtesy name Shanchang, was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daoyuan, courtesy name Shanchang, was from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史範之子。

translations.literal: He was son of Fan, Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Fan, governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 太和中，為尚書主客郎。

translations.literal: During the Taihe era he was Master of Guests in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he served as Master of Guests in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 御史中尉李彪以道元秉法清勤，引為治書侍御史。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Biao, because Daoyuan upheld the law with integrity and diligence, brought him in as Attendant Imperial Censor for Legal Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Biao, impressed by Daoyuan's integrity and diligence in upholding the law, appointed him Attendant Imperial Censor for Legal Documents.

sentences.zh: 累遷輔國將軍、東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He rose through posts to General Who Assists the State and Governor of Eastern Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Assists the State and governor of Eastern Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 威猛為治，蠻民詣闕訟其刻峻，坐免官。

translations.literal: He governed with fierce might; barbarian peoples came to the palace gate to sue over his severity and was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with fierce severity; the tribal peoples appealed to the throne against his harsh rule, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久之，行河南尹，尋即真。

translations.literal: After some time he acted as Intendant of Henan and soon received the full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he acted as Intendant of Henan and soon received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 肅宗以沃野、懷朔、薄骨律、武川、撫冥、柔玄、懷荒、禦夷諸鎮並改為州，其郡縣戍名令準古城邑。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong converted the garrisons of Woye, Huaishuo, Bogulü, Wuchuan, Fuming, Rouxuan, Huaihuang, and Yuyi into provinces; their commandery, county, and garrison names were ordered to follow ancient cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong converted the garrisons of Woye, Huaishuo, Bogulü, Wuchuan, Fuming, Rouxuan, Huaihuang, and Yuyi into provinces, ordering their administrative names to follow ancient place-names.

sentences.zh: 詔道元持節兼黃門侍郎，與都督李崇籌宜置立，裁減去留，儲兵積粟，以為邊備。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Daoyuan to hold the staff of authority and concurrently serve as Attendant of the Yellow Gate, together with Commander Li Chong to plan what should be established, decide reductions and retention, store troops and accumulate grain for frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Daoyuan commissioner with the staff of authority and concurrent Attendant of the Yellow Gate; together with Commander Li Chong he planned the new arrangements, decided what to retain or abolish, and stockpiled troops and grain for frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除安南將軍、御史中尉。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 道元素有嚴猛之稱。

translations.literal: Daoyuan had long borne a reputation for severity and fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan had long had a reputation for severity.

sentences.zh: 司州牧、汝南王悅嬖近左右丘念，常與臥起。

translations.literal: Governor of Si Province, Prince of Runan Yue, favored his close attendant Qiu Nian, who regularly slept and rose with him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue of Runan, governor of Si Province, favored his close attendant Qiu Nian, who regularly slept and rose with him.

sentences.zh: 及選州官，多由於念。

translations.literal: When selecting provincial officials, most went through Nian.
translations.idiomatic: Most provincial appointments went through Nian.

sentences.zh: 念匿於悅第，時還其家，道元收念付獄。

translations.literal: Nian hid in Yue's residence but sometimes returned home; Daoyuan seized Nian and handed him to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Nian hid in Yue's residence but sometimes went home; Daoyuan arrested him and threw him in prison.

sentences.zh: 悅啟靈太后請全之，敕赦之。

translations.literal: Yue petitioned Empress Dowager Ling to spare him; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue petitioned Empress Dowager Ling to spare him, and an edict ordered his release.

sentences.zh: 道元遂盡其命，因以劾悅。

translations.literal: Daoyuan thereupon ended his life and thereby impeached Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan executed him anyway and impeached Yue as well.

sentences.zh: 是時雍州刺史蕭寶夤反狀稍露，悅等諷朝廷遣為關右大使，遂為寶夤所害，死於陰盤驛亭。

translations.literal: At that time Governor of Yong Province Xiao Baoyin showed signs of rebellion; Yue and others insinuated to the court that he be sent as envoy to the Guanxi region, and he was killed by Baoyin at the Yingpan post station.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Baoyin, governor of Yong Province, showed signs of rebellion; Yue and others persuaded the court to send Daoyuan as envoy to the Guanxi region, and Baoyin killed him at the Yingpan post station.

sentences.zh: 道元好學，歷覽奇書。

translations.literal: Daoyuan loved learning and read through many rare books.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan loved learning and read widely among rare books.

sentences.zh: 撰注水經四十卷、本志十三篇，又為七聘及諸文，皆行於世。

translations.literal: He compiled a forty-juan commentary on the Water Classic and thirteen chapters of local records, and also wrote Seven Missions and other essays — all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a forty-juan commentary on the Water Classic and thirteen chapters of local records, as well as Seven Missions and other works, all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 然兄弟不能篤穆，又多嫌忌，時論薄之。

translations.literal: Yet the brothers could not be sincerely harmonious and were much given to suspicion; contemporary opinion looked down on them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the brothers were not harmonious and were much given to suspicion; contemporary opinion held them in low regard.

sentences.zh: 谷楷，昌黎人，濮陽公渾曾孫。

translations.literal: Gu Kai was a man of Changli, great-grandson of Duke of Puyang Hun.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Kai was from Changli, a great-grandson of Duke Hun of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 稍遷奉車都尉。

translations.literal: He gradually rose to Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: He gradually rose to Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.

sentences.zh: 時沙門法慶反於冀州，雖大軍討破，而妖帥尚未梟除。

translations.literal: At that time the monk Faqing rebelled in Ji Province; though the great army defeated him, the demonic chiefs had not yet been eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the monk Faqing rebelled in Ji Province; though the main army defeated him, the rebel leaders had not yet been eliminated.

sentences.zh: 詔楷詣冀州追捕，皆擒獲之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Kai to go to Ji Province to pursue and capture them — all were seized.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Kai to Ji Province to hunt them down; he captured them all.

sentences.zh: 楷眇一目而性甚嚴忍，前後奉使皆以酷暴為名。

translations.literal: Kai was blind in one eye and his nature was very stern and hard to bear; in missions before and after he was known for cruelty and violence.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was blind in one eye and by nature extremely harsh; on every mission he was known for cruelty.

sentences.zh: 時人號曰「瞎虎」。

translations.literal: People of the time called him "the blind tiger."
translations.idiomatic: People called him "the Blind Tiger."

sentences.zh: 尋為城門校尉，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Colonel of the City Gates and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Colonel of the City Gates and died in office.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：士之立名，其途不一，或以循良進，或以嚴酷顯。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: For a gentleman to establish a name, the paths are not one — some advance through dutiful goodness, some become prominent through severity and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: There are many paths by which a gentleman makes a name—some rise through dutiful administration, others become prominent through severity and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 故寬猛相資，德刑互設，然不嚴而化，君子所先。

translations.literal: Thus leniency and severity support each other, virtue and punishment are set in turn — yet to transform without severity is what the gentleman puts first.
translations.idiomatic: Leniency and severity complement each other, and virtue and punishment alternate—but transforming people without harshness is what the gentleman values most.

sentences.zh: 于洛侯等為惡不同，同歸於酷。

translations.literal: Yu Luohou and the others did evil in different ways, yet all alike ended in cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Luohou and the others did evil in different ways, yet all alike ended in cruelty.

sentences.zh: 肆其毒螫，多行殘忍。

translations.literal: They unleashed their venomous sting and often acted with cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: They unleashed their venom and often acted with cruelty.

sentences.zh: 賤人肌膚，同諸木石；

translations.literal: They debased human flesh and skin, treating it like wood and stone;
