translations.idiomatic: They held human flesh as cheap as wood and stone;

sentences.zh: 輕人性命，甚於芻狗。

translations.literal: they slighted human life, more than grass and dogs.
translations.idiomatic: they valued human life less than straw dogs.

sentences.zh: 長惡不悛，鮮有不及。

translations.literal: Nurturing evil without repentance, few did not come to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Persisting in evil without repentance, few escaped ruin.

sentences.zh: 故或身嬰罪戮，或憂恚顛隕。

translations.literal: Therefore some personally suffered punishment, some in grief and rage fell and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore some suffered execution themselves, others perished in grief and rage.

sentences.zh: [5]異途皆斃，各其宜焉。

translations.literal: [5] By different paths all perished — each as was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: [5] By different paths all perished—each as was fitting.

sentences.zh: 凡百君子，以為有天道矣。

translations.literal: All gentlemen considered that the Way of Heaven was at work.
translations.idiomatic: All thoughtful men took this as evidence that Heaven's justice was at work.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷八十九 諸本目錄注「闕」，但卷後無宋人校語。

translations.literal: Book of Wei, juan 89: Various editions' tables of contents mark it "missing," but there are no Song-dynasty collation notes after the juan.
translations.idiomatic: Book of Wei, juan 89: Various editions' tables of contents mark this juan as missing, but there are no Song-dynasty collation notes at the end of the scroll.

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云「魏收書亡，後人所補」，乃據目錄而言。

translations.literal: The Palace Edition textual verification says "Wei Shou's text is lost, supplemented by later people" — this is based on the table of contents.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Edition textual verification states that "Wei Shou's original text is lost and was supplemented by later editors"—a judgment based on the table of contents.

sentences.zh: 今按傳序與北史卷八七酷吏傳序不同，諸傳也多出入。

translations.literal: Now examining: the biography preface differs from Northern History juan 87, Biographies of Cruel Officials preface, and the individual biographies also diverge in many places.
translations.idiomatic: On examination, the preface differs from that in Northern History juan 87, Biographies of Cruel Officials, and the individual biographies also diverge in many places.

sentences.zh: 北史高遵傳

translations.literal: Northern History, biography of Gao Zun
translations.idiomatic: Northern History, biography of Gao Zun

sentences.zh: 〈附卷三一高允傳〉

translations.literal: 〈Attached juan 31, biography of Gao Yun〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Attached juan 31, biography of Gao Yun〉

sentences.zh: 、酈道元傳

translations.literal: , biography of Li Daoyuan
translations.idiomatic: , biography of Li Daoyuan

sentences.zh: 〈附卷二七酈範傳〉

translations.literal: 〈Attached juan 27, biography of Li Fan〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Attached juan 27, biography of Li Fan〉

sentences.zh: 均詳於此傳，谷楷傳則北史略去殺變亂人眾事。

translations.literal: are all detailed in this biography; the Northern History biography of Gu Kai omits the matter of killing the mutinous crowd.
translations.idiomatic: are all given in detail in this scroll; the Northern History biography of Gu Kai omits the account of killing the mutinous crowd.

sentences.zh: 此卷非以北史補甚明。

translations.literal: That this juan was not supplemented from the Northern History is quite clear.
translations.idiomatic: It is quite clear that this scroll was not supplemented from the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 但序甚簡短，高、酈二傳敍事較北史簡略。

translations.literal: But the preface is very brief, and the narratives of the Gao and Li biographies are more abbreviated than in the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: But the preface is very brief, and the Gao and Li biographies are more abbreviated than in the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 傳論全同北史，而北史實本隋書卷七四酷吏傳論，不過稍加改易而已，魏收豈能用隋書語，知是此傳襲取北史。

translations.literal: The biography conclusion is entirely the same as the Northern History, yet the Northern History in fact derives from Sui History juan 74, Biographies of Cruel Officials conclusion — only slightly altered. How could Wei Shou use Sui History language? It is known that this biography copied from the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: The concluding essay is identical to the Northern History, which in fact derives from the Sui History juan 74 essay on cruel officials with only slight alterations. Wei Shou could not have used Sui History language; this essay was clearly copied from the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 則此卷必非魏書原文，當是以高氏小史等書補，傳末校語偶脫。

translations.literal: Then this juan is certainly not the original Book of Wei text; it must have been supplemented from books such as the Gao clan Minor History — the collation note at the biography's end was occasionally lost.
translations.idiomatic: This scroll is therefore certainly not original Book of Wei text; it was likely supplemented from works such as the Gao clan Minor History, with the collation note at the end occasionally lost.

sentences.zh: 遂領逃連及諸畜牧者 張森楷云：「『逃連』字不可解，疑有誤。」

translations.literal: On the phrase "then led taolian and various herders": Zhang Senkai says, "The characters taolian are incomprehensible; there is suspected error."
translations.idiomatic: On the phrase "then led taolian and various herders": Zhang Senkai notes, "The term taolian is incomprehensible; the text is probably corrupt."

sentences.zh: 今臺使心協前事 北史卷八七張赦提傳「心協」作「止挾」。

translations.literal: Now the imperial envoy xinxie the earlier affair — Northern History juan 87, biography of Zhang Sheti: "xinxie" is written "zhi xie."
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial envoy xinxie the earlier affair — in Northern History juan 87, biography of Zhang Sheti, xinxie is written as zhi xie ("only harbored").

sentences.zh: 按「協」謂威脅，與文義不叶，疑作「挾」是。

translations.literal: According to this, "xie" means to threaten, which does not fit the text's meaning — it is suspected that "xie" (harbor) is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Here xie is taken to mean "threaten," which does not fit the context; xie ("harbor") is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 為司空令輔國長史 按司空屬官無令。

translations.literal: On the phrase "Chief Clerk Assisting the State under the Minister of Works": according to this, the Minister of Works had no "Director" among subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: On the phrase "Chief Clerk Assisting the State under the Minister of Works": the Minister of Works had no office titled "Director" among its subordinates.

sentences.zh: 「令」字疑衍，意謂以輔國將軍為司空長史。

translations.literal: The character "Director" is suspected to be a superfluous addition; the meaning is that as General Who Assists the State he served as Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The character ling ("Director") is probably a spurious addition; the meaning is that he served as Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works with the rank of General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 但亦晦澀，或有訛脫。

translations.literal: But this is also obscure; there may be corruption or omission.
translations.idiomatic: But the passage remains obscure; there may be further corruption or omission.

sentences.zh: 或憂恚顛隕 諸本「顛」作「值」，北史卷八七作「俱」，隋書卷七四酷吏傳論作「顛」。

translations.literal: On the phrase "or in grief and rage fell and perished": various editions write dian as zhi; Northern History juan 87 has ju; Sui History juan 74, Biographies of Cruel Officials conclusion has dian.
translations.idiomatic: On the phrase "or in grief and rage fell and perished": various editions read dian ("fall") as zhi; Northern History juan 87 has ju ("all"); Sui History juan 74 has dian.

sentences.zh: 按「值」字顯訛，「俱」字雖可通，然「顛隕」與上句「罪戮」對文，今據隋書改。

translations.literal: According to this, the character zhi is clearly erroneous; ju, though passable, yet dianyun pairs with the preceding clause zuilü in parallel structure — now following the Sui History for the correction.
translations.idiomatic: The reading zhi is clearly erroneous; ju is possible but dianyun ("fall and perish") parallels zuilü ("suffer punishment") in the preceding clause; the text is corrected here following the Sui History.
